ok_forty_foot_hole_routes.blurb: Forty Foot Hole Routes is a small cluster of thirteen climbs in the short canyon known as Forty Foot Hole, inside the Wichita Mountains Wildlife Refuge of southwest Oklahoma. It is almost entirely traditional climbing, with one bolted line, one top-rope and a single mixed-style entry. Grades are friendly at the bottom: about half the routes sit at 5.7 or 5.8, then the range steps up through a 5.10 and two 5.11s to one 5.12. Walls are short and compact, so a standard rack of nuts and cams does the work, and the canyon makes for a quick half-day outing with a mixed-ability group.

ok_04_headwall.blurb: The Headwall is a granite wall on Quartz Mountain in the Wichita range of southwest Oklahoma, the third of the mountain's big formations and visible from the parking area. Twelve routes are recorded here: mostly trad, four bolted lines and one aid route. The grades lean hard. A handful of easy-to-moderate leads at 5.6 and 5.8 give way to a few 5.10s and 5.11s, and 5.12 is the most common level, topped by a 5.13. Expect bold, friction-dependent face climbing on this mountain, and note that the sun reaches most of the rock for much of the day, which makes cooler months the comfortable choice.

ok_desperate_dome_desperate_reality_clif.blurb: Desperate Dome, also called Desperate Reality Cliff, is a short granite cliff in Charon's Gardens, part of the Wichita Mountains Wildlife Refuge in southwest Oklahoma. Of its twelve routes, ten are traditional, mostly crack climbs, with one bolted line and one top-rope. The grades cluster in the 5.10s, with several 5.11s, a single 5.12 and a few easier leads from 5.7 to 5.9. The stone is coarse and crystalline, so tape up for the cracks. The cliff faces northeast and keeps its shade for much of the day, a plus in warm weather. The walk in takes roughly twenty to twenty-five minutes, and the faint path can be hard to follow.

ok_dog_wall.blurb: Dog Wall is one of the walls in Treasure Cove, a rocky gully off Charon's Gardens in the Wichita Mountains Wildlife Refuge of southwest Oklahoma. Twelve routes are listed, mostly traditional lines on granite, plus one bolted route, one top-rope and two aid climbs. Free climbs run from 5.6 to 5.10 and bunch up around 5.9, which suits a leader happy on moderate gear routes. Getting in is the main commitment: a long hike followed by steep third-class scrambling up the slab or boulders. The cove sees few visitors and is considered a good place to climb in winter.

ok_low_angle_wall_boulder.blurb: Low Angle Wall Boulder is a boulder about the size of a house in Robbers Cave State Park, in southeast Oklahoma, a short walk beyond the prominent Mushroom Boulder. The front is gently angled and knobby; the back is covered in pockets and buckets and attracts wasps. Twelve climbs are recorded: seven trad lines, two top-rope routes and three easy slab problems at V0. Free routes run from 5.5 to 5.10, with most at 5.8 or 5.9. The sandstone here is dense and solid enough to protect with nuts and cams, so it is a handy spot for beginners practicing gear placement or top-roping.

ok_the_keystones.blurb: The Keystones are a dozen sandstone boulders on the lake shore just southwest of Keystone Dam, in the Tulsa area of Oklahoma. This is bouldering only, with problems from V1 to V6, most of them between V3 and V5, so it fits climbers who already have some experience on rock. The stone is generally good quality. To reach the blocks, drop down the angler's path to the water and then work northwest along the shoreline from boulder to boulder. The boulders can be seen from the road, and the setting is open lakeside rather than a deep forest.

ok_east_face.blurb: East Face is the sunrise side of the Crab Eyes formation in Charon's Gardens, within the Wichita Mountains Wildlife Refuge of southwest Oklahoma. Eleven of its twelve routes are traditional crack climbs, and one is a top-rope. There is little at the easy end: a lone 5.8, two 5.9s, four 5.10s and five routes in the 5.12 range. Climbs run up to about seventy feet, with offwidth sections on some. The east side is regarded as the place to find shade here, so it is a sensible choice when the other walls are baking in the sun.
